# Hassles format conformance BASELINE v1

This is an offline, test-only baseline, **NOT full parity** or Calendar-provider proof. Canonical file: `internal/hassles/testdata/format-contract-v1.json`; Android vendors its exact bytes at `android/app/src/test/resources/format-contract-v1.json`. No runtime cross-repository lookup. SHA-256 is pinned independently in each test and comparator. Goldens are declarative, source-audited expectations, not compiler output; independent review remains required.

## Coverage

185 explicit named cases: 94 schedule cross-product cases (once × work; daily/weekly/monthly/yearly × 1/2/999 × work × UNTIL; weekdays × work × UNTIL; nine hourly choices × work × UNTIL; four additional half-hour :47 phases), 43 validation boundaries, and 48 imports (28 required base IDs plus essential variants and four recurrence witnesses). IDs are the inventory; no invisible fixture loops. All 335 known differing paths have exact values, reasons and source references. Matching supplied occurrences does NOT establish native provider expansion equivalence.

## Strict schema

UTF-8 JSON, no unknown fields; `schemaVersion:1`, `contractId:"hassles-format-v1"`, `cases:[...]`. Unique nonempty case IDs; every case must be consumed exactly once. Fields of a case:

- `id`, `kind` (`schedule` or `import`), `now` (fixed RFC3339 UTC), `actions`, `nativeInstances`, `expected`, `differences` are required.
- Schedule cases additionally require `schedule` (production Schedule fields: title, start, timeZone, cadence, interval, until, workHours); imports instead require nonempty `events`.
- Event required fields: `key`, `uid`, `description`, `title`, `dtstart`, `durationSeconds` (integer or null), `alarmMinutes`, `attendees` (email strings), `etagStrength` (`strong` or `weak`). Optional: `dtend`, `rrule`, `rdate`, `exdate`, `organizer`, `detachedFrom`. Keys unique. No unspecified event flags.
- Typed dates: `{type:"DATE",raw:"YYYYMMDD"}`, `{type:"UTC",raw:"YYYYMMDDTHHmmssZ"}`, or `{type:"LOCAL",raw:"YYYYMMDDTHHmmss",tzid:"IANA zone"}`. Lists use these same objects; comma-separated raw text remains raw (including duplicates). No BYSECOND repair, discarded rule keys, ownership inference, or recurrence expansion in adapters.
- Instances: `{eventKey,begin,end}`, RFC3339 UTC, explicit provider evidence; preserve all ties. Empty is deliberately unknown for recurring native rows, NOT ended. Do not filter supplied witnesses using a clock window: the corpus explicitly supplies evidence (some witnesses illustrate beyond-window semantics).
- `differences:[{path,web,android,reason,source:[...]}]`: JSON pointers to exact existing observation leaves, never wildcards. Both values must differ; web equals the common expected baseline at that path. Both runners assert their platform override, all other leaves assert the common baseline. Missing/new leaves, unused/converged/stale differences fail. Null is a real leaf; never omit it. Arrays, when present in observations, are atomic leaves.

## Import adapters (not compilers)

Use synthetic UUID `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`, collection `/format/`, account/owner `owner@fixture.invalid`, calendar ID 1. Input description is literal: `[docket]` and UUID markers are not inferred from recognition or account equality. Raw title, description, UID, RRULE, exclusions and recurrence-date spellings are retained.

Web constructs ical.Calendar/Event directly (VERSION 2.0, synthetic PRODID), path `/format/<key>.ics`, strong ETag `"fixture-<key>"` or weak `W/"fixture-<key>"`. Add SUMMARY, UID, DESCRIPTION, DTSTAMP set to the fixed case.now (required VEVENT serialization evidence), raw typed DTSTART, optional raw typed DTEND; otherwise DURATION `PT<durationSeconds>S` when nonnull. Add raw RRULE and typed RDATE/EXDATE properties, actual ATTENDEE/ORGANIZER properties when supplied. Add a DISPLAY alarm with TRIGGER `PT0S` or `-PT<alarmMinutes>M`. No METHOD, cancellation or VTIMEZONE. Add synthetic root `X-FORMAT-OPAQUE:root` and event `X-FORMAT-OPAQUE:event-<key>` to check raw preservation separately from equality. For a detached event, append its VEVENT into the referenced master's resource, set RECURRENCE-ID to its typed start; retain master's ETag/path. Do not expose it as a second resource.

Android constructs EventRow, CalendarBinding and CalendarSnapshot directly. Event IDs are 1-based input indices; calendar_id=1. Binding has access=500, maxReminders=1, reminders="1", visible=true, sync=false, account/owner `owner@fixture.invalid`, type="LOCAL", name="Synthetic format". Present OwnerContext and OrganizerWitness(OTHER) are safe defaults; organizer is empty, unsynced. A supplied nonempty organizer stays nonempty with OTHER role (not SELF). All other safe fields: deleted="0", eventStatus="1", availability="1", hasAlarm="1", hasAttendeeData reflects actual attendee rows, _sync_id empty, original links empty; uid2445=input UID. Include a synthetic protected field `customAppPackage:"fixture.invalid"`. Exactly one reminder `{minutes:<alarmMinutes>,method:"1"}`; actual attendee rows from input. These defaults supply explicit owner/role/status evidence, not inferred ownership.

Map DATE to UTC midnight epoch and allDay="1", timezone Melbourne; UTC DATE-TIME to its epoch and eventTimezone="UTC"; LOCAL to epoch using its literal TZID and eventTimezone=<tzid>, allDay="0". DTEND maps likewise. If no explicit DTEND and durationSeconds nonnull: once uses epoch+seconds DTEND and empty DURATION; recurring uses `PT<seconds>S` DURATION and empty DTEND. Never adjust unsupported eight-minute durations. RDATE/EXDATE raw values joined by comma (no conversion of local completion text to UTC). `detachedFrom` sets original_id to referenced index; it remains a provider row. No ETag analogue is invented. Use all explicitly supplied native Instances with their original begin/end.

## Observations and independent actions

Schedule observation: `validation:{accepted:boolean}`, `emission:null|{start:<UTC RFC3339>,timeZone,durationSeconds,cadence,interval,until,workHours,rule:{KEY:raw-value}}`, `actions:{create:<action>}`. Emission comes from actual NewCalendar/compile output, normalized schedule fields from actual recognized output; rule key order alone is immaterial. Keep BY-list spelling/order exact. Invalid validation has null emission and actual denied create with zero writes.

Import observation: `validation:{accepted:null}` (not a Schedule validation input), `profile:{recognized,cadence,interval,until,workHours}` (unsupported => false plus four nulls), `capabilities:{edit,titleOnly,instance,allDelete}`, `timing:{knowledge,next,last,allDay}`, `actions:{edit,titleOnly,instance,all}`. Web profile uses Inventory task.Schedule, Android profile uses selected first input master's recognize/task.schedule. The web group/native per-row difference is explicitly allowlisted, not hidden by regrouping. Select task containing first input key `a` (native first row ID 1). Capabilities reflect production authorization, not only recognition. Timing comes from actual Inventory/rows, state `upcoming|past|unknown`, next/last UTC RFC3339 or null, allDay true iff either actual next/last all-day flag; native all-day flag is row timing.nextAllDay. Report metadata `timingAuthority` is pinned to `web-evaluation` or `native-instances`, respectively. Authority is NOT compared as a format-gap leaf and does not claim provider expansion equivalence.

Every action uses a freshly reconstructed input, current inventory revision/native original fingerprint, original target and witness. Create uses fixture Schedule and fixed UUID. Full edit uses `{title:"Edited synthetic task",start:"2026-01-12T15:17",timeZone:"Australia/Melbourne",cadence:"daily",interval:2,until:"",workHours:false}`. Title-only uses original recognized schedule with only title changed to `Edited synthetic task`; if unsupported supply the fixed edit Schedule and let production deny. Web maps instance to done-instance (non-null at/token; empty strings if unavailable, dryRun=false) and all to delete. Native uses instance/all. No preceding action may grant a later action eligibility.

Action leaves: `{accepted,writes,effect,target,witness,preserved}`. `writes` counts actual backend/gateway writes (web group deletion can be two). `effect` = none/create/update/exclude/delete; denied => none, zero writes, empty target, null witness. `target` = new for create, otherwise sorted resource/input keys joined with commas (detached deletion targets master a). `witness` is only an accepted instance's ORIGINAL selected UTC instant; otherwise null. Inspect actual write plans/bodies, do not copy these leaves from the expected value. Native repository execution uses an in-memory gateway/storage; no device/provider. On supported saves assert actual saved reminder, and separately prove wrong-reminder verification fails.

`preserved` is an independently checked mutation invariant, not shared opaque-byte equality. Denied: zero writes and identical input raw fingerprint. Create: saved title, duration and zero alarm correct. Full edit: UID, original target, opaque fields, notes, existing exclusions and alarms survive. Title-only: every property/field except title and write timestamps unchanged. Recurring instance: original DTSTART, UID, target, opaque data and all other fields unchanged except appended EXDATE + completion marker + write timestamps; no exception insertion; appended UTC instant equals original witness. Once instance: delete original resource only. All: delete original selected resource(s) only, conditional ETag/original native evidence retained. Revision tokens, provider IDs, ETags and encoded calendars are checked locally, never claimed equal across platforms.

## Known defect, not intended compatibility policy

`timing-dst-gap-current-daily` deliberately records a **KNOWN RFC SEMANTIC BUG**: generic Go DAILY iteration normalizes the nonexistent Melbourne 2026-10-04 02:30 to 03:30, instead of RFC gap-skipping. Its last=2026-10-03T16:30:00Z is the current-source baseline, not a desired behavior or parity claim. Native past remains unknown and the supplied next is not provider-expansion proof. The separate `boundary-overlap-before` five-minute creation golden remains durationSeconds=300 and preserved=true: unsafe 65-minute creation must FAIL, never become an allowlisted policy difference. Owner-approved exception: `ApplySchedule` now writes DTEND as UTC, explicitly removing stale DTEND TZID while retaining DTSTART Melbourne and other protected fields; its existing title-only early return preserves raw local DTEND. This fixes the creation/full-edit duration defect, NOT the generic DAILY gap iterator defect tracked in [zpm/chainmail#381](https://github.com/zachpmanson/chainmail/issues/381). Three supported hourly/work imports exercise actual full/title/instance/all mutations and obsolete work/hourly metadata removal.

## Reports and local command

Opt-in `HASSLES_CONFORMANCE_REPORT=/absolute/file.json`. Exact report fields: `{schemaVersion:1,contractId:"hassles-format-v1",corpusSha256:<lowercase hex>,platform:"web"|"android",timingAuthority:"web-evaluation"|"native-instances",generatedAt:<current RFC3339 UTC>,passed:boolean,consumedCaseCount:<integer>,cases:[{id,passed:boolean,observation:<actual observation>}]}`. No expected clones, inventory logs or private data. Report freshness <=1 hour; generatedAt must not precede that checkout's corpus mtime. Reports compare declared semantics only.

```sh
# In web checkout (offline cached Nix/toolchain/dependencies):
HASSLES_CONFORMANCE_REPORT=/tmp/web-format.json GOMAXPROCS=4 nix develop --command go test -p 2 ./internal/hassles -run '^TestFormatConformance' -count=1
# In native checkout:
HASSLES_CONFORMANCE_REPORT=/tmp/android-format.json nix develop --command make format-conformance
nix develop --command python3 scripts/check-hassles-format-conformance.py --web /absolute/web --android /absolute/native --web-report /tmp/web-format.json --android-report /tmp/android-format.json
nix develop --command python3 scripts/check-hassles-format-conformance.py --self-test
```

The web development shell includes Python for this standard-library-only test comparator; no runtime package dependency is added. Comparator only reads explicit local checkouts/reports. It never builds, fetches or contacts Calendar/network. Successful known-gap output must say `PASS: shared contract; NOT full parity (N known differing paths)`. Baseline gaps include unsupported-owned deletion, reminder policy, legacy/malformed UUID ownership, grouping, explicit WKST, local completion exclusions, weak ETags, timing knowledge (authority is report metadata). No production changes beyond the explicitly owner-approved narrow UTC-DTEND duration fix are authorized; no dependency/APK/CI changes. OEM storage, provider expansion, remote CAS/sync/notifications and credentials are outside this baseline.
